- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model tends to overestimate mean reversion — adjust downward by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply 2–5% downward bias to first 5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., > 0.3 for 3+ days), model underestimates upside — add 3–7% upward bias to forecast.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment reversal — if sentiment turns negative after a positive run, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility — smooth out extreme swings by reducing standard deviation by 15–25% in forecast.
